# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 52 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 52 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_052_page_001.jpg

---

## Council Notes

Similitude 3 is brief but theologically pointed. The winter-trees image makes the argument that moral differentiation is not yet visible in the present age (*aiōn*). This is Hermas's version of the parable of the wheat and tares (Matt 13:24-30): the separation will come in summer/the age to come (developed in Similitude 4).

The identification of "this present age" as "winter for the righteous" is a striking claim. The righteous are at their most invisible — stripped of what makes them distinct — in the current era. This may be an implicit theodicy: why do the righteous seem to suffer like sinners? Because it is winter for everyone.

EMET and LOGOS both handle the "dry/withered" vocabulary. SOPHIA uses "dry" to distinguish from "withered" — Hermas uses the visual appearance of dryness as the unifying feature of the winter trees.

---

## Similitude 3 — Trees in Winter

**52:1** He showed me many trees without leaves, which appeared to me to be dry; for they all looked alike. And he said to me: "Do you see these trees?" "I see them, lord," I replied; "they all look alike and are dry." He answered and said to me: "These trees that you see are those who dwell in this present age."

**52:2** "Why then, lord," I asked, "do they appear dry and all alike?" "Because," he said, "neither the righteous nor sinners are distinguishable in this present age, but they all resemble one another. For this present age is winter for the righteous who dwell in it, and they are not distinguishable among the sinners.

**52:3** For just as in winter the trees, having shed their leaves, all look alike, and it is not apparent which are withered and which are alive — so too in this present age neither the righteous nor sinners are apparent, but all appear alike to one another."

---

*SOPHIA represents the consensus rendering of EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA, with rulings recorded in the Disagreement Log.*
